bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

Whether you are planning your finances, negotiating a pay rise, or comparing your earnings to international benchmarks such as the average salary philippines, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure is a fundamental skill. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, and most salary calculations are based on this assumption.

### The Basic Formula

The formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation is:

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay would be $30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This figure does not include superannuation, which is paid on top by your employer.

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. So a weekly pay of $1,140 (based on $30.00 per hour for 38 hours) gives a fortnightly gross of $2,280. Knowing your fortnightly amount can help with budgeting and loan applications.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making their minimum rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave.

Many employees are covered by award rates, which are industry-specific minimum pay rates set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. These rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. You can find the relevant pay guide for your industry on the [pay guides](/blog) page. Award rates may also include penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, or late shifts, which are not accounted for in the basic conversion formula.

### Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings data. As of May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week. For all employees (including part-time), the average was $1,579.20 per week. These are averages across all industries and states, not the median for a specific job. If you are comparing your pay to these figures, remember that your role may differ significantly. The ABS data provides a useful benchmark, but your actual pay depends on your occupation, experience, and location.

### Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds for 2026–27 were not confirmed at the time of this article, so the calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. This may affect your estimated take-home pay slightly, but the difference is usually small.

### Superannuation

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual salary is $100,000, your employer must contribute an additional $12,000 to your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra benefit that grows over time for your retirement.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) tool helps you convert your hourly rate to annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Enter your base hourly rate (do not include casual loading in the rate itself). If you are a casual employee, check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. The calculator then estimates your gross pay, tax, Medicare, and superannuation. Remember that it assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work different hours, you can manually adjust using the formula above.

### International Comparisons

When looking at international benchmarks such as the average salary philippines, it is important to consider differences in cost of living, tax systems, and social security. The conversion formula remains the same, but the purchasing power of your Australian dollar may differ. Use the calculator to get your annual figure, then adjust for local conditions. For example, the average salary philippines is often quoted in Philippine pesos, so you would need to convert currencies and account for different tax rates and living expenses.

### Important Notes

The annual pay shown here is based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, refer to our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.
